chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi and Uqba, both together, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation. So He created those whom He loved from what He loved, and what He loved was that He created it from the clay of Paradise; and He created those whom He hated from what He hated, and what He hated was that He created it from the clay of the Fire. Then He sent them into the shadows.
So I asked: 'And what are the shadows?' He said: 'Have you not seen your shadow in the sun — it is something, yet it is not a thing?'
Then He sent Prophets from among them, and they invited them to the acknowledgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic — and that is His word, Mighty and Majestic:
"And if you ask them who created them, they would certainly say: Allah." [43:87]

Then they invited them to the acknowledgment of the Prophets; some acknowledged and some denied. Then they invited them to our Wilayah, and, by God, the one who loved acknowledged it, and the one who hated denied it. And that is His word:
"But they were not going to believe in what they had belied before." [10:74]
Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The denial was there (at that time).'

key_terms.التَّكْذِيبُ: The denial/belying — the pre-eternal rejection of Wilayah by those created from the clay of Fire
key_terms.الظِّلَال: The shadows/realm of shadows ('alam al-zill) — a pre-physical intermediate realm where souls existed in shadow form before entering the physical world
key_terms.الْإِقْرَار: Acknowledgment/recognition — the formal acceptance of God's sovereignty, Prophethood, and Imamate
key_terms.طِينَةُ النَّارِ: Clay of Fire — the primordial substance from which despised souls were formed
key_terms.طِينَةُ الْجَنَّةِ: Clay of Paradise — the primordial substance from which beloved souls were formed
key_terms.وَلَايَتِنَا: Our Wilayah — the divinely ordained authority and guardianship of the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the creation of souls from the clay of Paradise and Fire in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates a cosmological teaching about the pre-eternal differentiation of souls: those beloved by God were created from the clay of Paradise, while those despised were created from the clay of Fire. God then sent them into the realm of shadows ('alam al-zill) — the pre-physical world of forms — and thereafter raised Prophets to invite them to acknowledge God, the Prophets, and ultimately the Wilayah (divinely appointed guardianship) of the Ahl al-Bayt. The hadith anchors the Shia doctrine of divine predetermination in a primordial covenant, explaining that those who reject Wilayah in this life had already rejected it in the pre-existential realm — their denial is thus a continuation of ancient opposition rooted in the nature of their clay.
